sections.heading: Wishing with ojalá
sections.body: *Ojalá* (from Arabic, "may God will it") means "I hope / let's hope / if only" and is **always** followed by the subjunctive. *Que* is optional after it: *Ojalá (que) llueva mañana.* (I hope it rains tomorrow.) *¡Ojalá!* on its own means "I hope so!"

sections.heading: Wanting and hoping that someone else…
sections.body:
When one person wants, hopes, or wishes something about **another** person or thing, use *que* + subjunctive:

- *querer que*: *Quiero que vengas.*
- *esperar que* (to hope): *Espero que estés bien.* (I hope you're well.)
- *desear que* (to wish, more formal): *Te deseo que tengas un buen viaje.*
- *preferir que*: *Prefiero que me llames mañana.*

If the subject is the same, use the infinitive: *Espero llegar a tiempo.* (I hope to arrive on time.) vs. *Espero que llegues a tiempo.* (I hope you arrive on time.)

sections.heading: Wishes as set phrases
sections.body: Many good wishes are really *(Espero) que* + subjunctive with the first part left out — you know some already: *¡Que te mejores!* (Get well!) *¡Que te vaya bien!* *¡Que tengas un buen día!* (Have a good day!) *¡Que descanses!* (Sleep well / rest up!) *¡Que lo pases bien!* (Have a good time!) *¡Que cumplas muchos más!*

examples: I hope you pass the exam.
Espero que te guste el regalo.
I hope you like the gift.
Te deseo que tengas un buen viaje.
I wish you a good trip.
I'd rather you call me tomorrow.
I hope to arrive on time.
I hope you arrive on time.
¡Que lo pases bien en la fiesta!
Have a good time at the party!
Mis padres esperan que yo sea médico.
My parents hope I'll be a doctor.
Hopefully there won't be much traffic.
I'd prefer that you don't come today.
